data.title: CFTC staff say bitcoin, ether can count toward derivatives firms’ operating expenses
data.description:
Staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an advisory saying certain regulated clearinghouses and exchanges may count cryptocurrencies such as bitcoin and ether toward a requirement to maintain enough assets to cover at least one year of operating expenses.

On Monday, the agency's Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk released that advisory and said ether, bitcoin, and payment stablecoins could be counted toward that requirement — and would be subject to a haircut — a regulatory discount applied to their market value to account for potential losses.

"Pleased to see @CFTC staff continue to provide important clarity around crypto assets in US derivatives markets through today’s staff advisory," said CFTC Chair Michael Selig in a post on X.

The advisory applies to swap execution facilities, clearing organizations and designated contract markets. It also does not create new legal obligations and is not enforceable. The CFTC also noted that crypto do not qualify as cash or very liquid securities under the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles — the set of accounting rules used by U.S. companies to report financial statements — so they are not eligible towards a liquidity requirement, which is separate.

Katherine Kirkpatrick Bos, Chainlink Labs' head of legal, called the advisory "significant."

"People don't realize that one of the impediments to these licenses is the cost of holding a lot of $ - this will help," she said in a post on X.

Also on Monday, the CFTC published its final rule creating a reporting framework for certain event contracts. Rulemaking was necessary, the CFTC said, because the agency had previously moved through a no-action letter process and those don't carry the "force of law," and it also wanted to standardize reported data.

The final rule adds a new part regarding clarifying dates for compliance.

“The CFTC will no longer regulate market participants through a patchwork of no-action letters, which serve as band-aids for unworkable regulations," Selig said in a statement. "This final rule is an important step in future-proofing the regulatory framework for event contracts."

data.title: What are the various US federal and state probes faced by Nvidia and Jensen Huang?
data.description:
By Kanishka Singh

As President Donald Trump welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO and declared the tech billionaire's return posed no national security risk, the company and its boss faced a host of state and federal probes and reviews.

Here are details on some of those actions, with their status in certain cases remaining unclear:

FBI AND US INTELLIGENCE REVIEWS:

After reports that the Nvidia CEO had an extramarital affair with unrelated Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US intelligence agencies probed over whether she was a Chinese asset, Trump said on November 9 the FBI was "looking into" the issue.

Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, but has not ​publicly addressed the situation further. China has denied the espionage allegations.

US intelligence agencies examined the extent of the Chinese businesswoman's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, people familiar with the matter have told Reuters.

When asked after the Nvidia CEO's reinstatement what the CIA had told Trump, the president told CNBC: "Let me just say, I have clearance. And if I didn't have clearance, I wouldn't have done ​the deal (with Nvidia's board for Jensen Huang's return)."

Trump said Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the federal government has no evidence that Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

The New York Times reported that Alice Huang kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during the affair. China's foreign ministry has previously said the spy accusations were "groundless," and Reuters has been unable to determine Alice Huang's whereabouts to seek comment.

Nvidia's board has formed a committee to investigate ​whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Jensen Huang and is also starting a search to name a new chief compliance officer.

ANTITRUST PROBE:

The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's $12.9 billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported in October.

The ‌Justice Department's recent questioning covers Nvidia's acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and whether the chip designer has exerted pressure on its customers, people familiar with the matter said in October.

The Justice Department has also scrutinized Nvidia's ​conduct following other transactions, including ⁠its 2025 deal to license technology from chip startup Groq and hire its engineers, Reuters has reported.

Officials have explored whether Nvidia unfairly offered larger allocations of AI chips if customers purchased its networking equipment and Groq processors, raising questions about whether Nvidia used its dominant product to push into a newer market.

Nvidia, which is a cornerstone ​of the tech economy and AI boom, has declined to comment on the probes.

SEC PROBE:

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, Reuters reported on November 20, citing two people briefed on the matter.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its ​inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog examined.

Analysts and investors have grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers.

Nvidia has backed AI companies and cloud providers ​and provided guarantees connected to data-center projects that use its equipment. Critics say such arrangements can make it harder for investors to assess ​the quality of chipmakers' revenue ⁠and their true financial exposure.

On its November 17 earnings call, Nvidia's then-interim CEO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more ⁠selective about future AI industry financing deals.

CALIFORNIA STATE PROBE:

California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on November 19 his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia related to reports of Huang's affair with the Chinese businesswoman.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia's actions violated California law, the attorney general's office said.

CONGRESSIONAL PROBES:

Democrats, who will hold a majority in the House of Representatives and the Senate from January following the November midterm elections, have been very critical of Huang and Nvidia and of Huang's ties to the Republican president. US ‌lawmakers from both parties sharply criticized Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang as CEO.

"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain," top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer said after Huang was reinstated.

Top House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries said Congress will "not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by Nvidia."

Huang has voiced support for Trump's AI agenda and met the Republican leader many times as Nvidia has sought to sell advanced chips to the ‌Chinese market and lobbied for looser restrictions on Chinese access to Nvidia's sophisticated AI chips.

Democratic and Republican lawmakers have called to halt exports of advanced AI chips to China. Huang and the White House have argued that continuing US sales to China would keep Chinese customers reliant on US technology.

Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing on December 3, the Senate Banking Committee said.

The chairs of the House committees on China, intelligence and foreign affairs separately said Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter have confirmed they will appear for transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as previously planned.

MEGASPEED PROBES:

Democratic lawmakers have opened a probe into what influence Nvidia was able to wield over a US Commerce Department investigation of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed for possible illegal diversion of chips to China, according ‌to a November 19 letter reviewed by Reuters.

The Chinese businesswoman with whom the Nvidia boss had an affair is a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that operates data centers. Megaspeed said it complies with all applicable laws, including US ⁠export control ​requirements.

Nvidia said that as an American ​company it consults with department officials to answer questions, provide information and request guidance.

The Commerce and ​Justice departments released information on November 16 about Washington's investigation into Megaspeed, Nvidia's Asia-Pacific partner, which the departments said ‌began two years ago.

They said Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia ​in May 2025 about sales to the company and, with Singaporean authorities, conducted an ​on-site inspection in June 2025 at Megaspeed and interviewed Alice Huang.

Washington added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist on November 23.

data.title: Aland Equity Group Receives First Recurring Management Fee from Elm Grove Fund
data.description:
Aland Equity Group has received its first $374,000 management fee from the Aland Elm Grove Estate Fund following shareholder approval of the management rights agreement.

The payment begins a scheduled $3.366 million fee stream, including the amount received, that the group expects to collect in monthly instalments.

Additional investment returns are expected to bring the combined proceeds from Elm Grove to approximately $4.1m once the associated residential lot sales are completed.

The transaction moves Aland’s capital-light property funds strategy from establishing management rights to receiving revenue, as it targets profitability in the 2027 financial year.

Monthly Fees Begin Flowing

The fund covers the marketing and sale of 56 residential lots at Elm Grove Heights in Bungendore, New South Wales, a development previously identified as Aland’s first application of its capital-light model.

Aland launched the fund in October with the management rights acquisition still conditional on shareholder approval at its annual general meeting.

That approval has now been obtained, allowing the first fee payment to be made under the agreed arrangements.

Unlike the investment returns linked to lot sales, the management fees are scheduled to arrive progressively through the remainder of the financial year.

Lot Sales Underpin Returns

Aland is the fund’s sole investor, and expects to receive approximately $725,000 in additional investment returns after fund costs, with all 56 lot sales expected to be completed by 30 June 2027 and the final fund distributions anticipated shortly after that date.

The earlier fund arrangements provide for management rights over the residential lots without requiring the fund to purchase the underlying land upfront.

This structure is intended to limit the capital committed to property ownership while allowing Aland to earn management fees and participate in fund returns.

The forecast $4.1m combined return remains dependent on the scheduled fees and completion of the lot sales, rather than representing cash already received.

Larger Development in View

Elm Grove is intended to provide an operating model for the much larger Chinnerys Precinct, which Aland plans to commence in 2027.

The proposed precinct encompasses approximately 3,200 residential lots and would provide management fees and investment returns over several years.

Aland has previously outlined an indicative income opportunity at Chinnerys based on assumed lot sales, although those estimates depend on future project activity.

For now, the first Elm Grove receipt provides a tangible start to the group’s property management income while the remaining fee payments and land sales proceed.

data.title: Japan's factory activity expands in November, PMI shows
data.description:
Japan's manufacturing activity grew at a slightly faster in November as output and export orders picked up on semiconductor and electronics demand, a preliminary business survey showed on Tuesday.

  • The S&P Global Flash Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 53.7 in November from 53.3 in October, a preliminary survey by S&P Global showed. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction.

  • A key sub-index for factory output grew and new orders rose at a solid pace helped by a sharp rise in export orders.

  • New export orders accelerated from October thanks to robust demand, especially from other major Asian economies. This lifted new export business at the overall private sector at the fastest rate since January 2018.

  • Manufacturers were more optimistic than service providers about the business outlook, but confidence in both sectors weakened from October on worries about rising costs, labour shortages and concerns over a slowdown in consumer spending.

  • Price pressures remained strong across the private sector even as they eased. Input cost inflation slowed to an eight-month low, while output charge inflation weakened to its lowest since March, though both stayed historically sharp.

  • "Japan's private sector continued to expand midway through the final quarter of the year, but momentum was lost amid a slowdown in service sector activity," said Annabel Fiddes, Economics Associate Director at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

  • "Uncertainty remains elevated as firms grapple with sharply rising costs and worries over a sustained slowdown in consumer spending."

  • The services sector weakened, with the flash Japan services PMI slipping to 50.5 from 51.7.

  • The composite PMI, which combines manufacturing and services, eased to 51.5, a six-month low, from 52.1 in October.

data.title: Japan's Nikkei rises over 3% after Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
data.description:
By Satoshi Sugiyama

Japan's Nikkei share average climbed more than 3% on Tuesday, tracking a sharp rally on Wall Street as Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO rekindled investor enthusiasm for the AI trade.

The Nikkei 225 Index advanced 3.22% to 58,254.82, rebounding from Friday's 5% decline. The broader Topix climbed 2.07% to 3,750.45, reversing Friday's nearly 4% drop. Tokyo markets were closed on Monday for a public holiday.

Shares of Nvidia , a bellwether for the AI sector, surged 31.5% overnight in their biggest one-day percentage gain since May 9, 2003.

The chipmaker had announced Huang's resignation on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy, a development that helped trigger last week's global equity selloff.

(00:26 GMT) StarHub to Acquire Singapore Telecom Operator in All Share Deal

By P.R. Venkat

StarHub will acquire Singapore telecom operator M1 in an all-share deal valuing it at 1.36 billion Singapore dollars, equivalent to US$1.05 billion.

Shareholders of M1, which is controlled by Keppel Ltd., will be issued about 651.7 million new Starhub shares, which represents about 27.4% of the enlarged company, the three companies said in a joint statement Tuesday.

Keppel will effectively hold 23.0% and become a substantial shareholder of StarHub, and has agreed to keep its stake for at least 12 months.

The remaining 4.4% stake will be held by M1's other shareholders.

After the merger, the combined group will have 4.1 million customers and about S$2.6 billion in annual revenue.

data.title: Singapore Raises 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to Around 6%
data.description:
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Revised 3Q GDP +1.5% Adj Q/Q vs +1.1% Earlier Estimate
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Revised 3Q GDP +6.1% on Year vs +5.4% Earlier Estimate
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Raises 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to Around 6.0% From 4.5%-5.5% Previously
(00:00 GMT) *Singapore Expects 2027 GDP Growth Forecast of 2.5%-4.5%
(00:15 GMT) Singapore Raises 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to Around 6%

By Amanda Lee

SINGAPORE--Singapore raised its economic growth forecast for the year following stronger-than-estimated third-quarter growth, though it cautioned that global headwinds persist.

Gross domestic product expanded 6.1% in the July-September period from a year earlier, according to revised data released Tuesday. The figure was above the 5.4% advance estimate released in October.

Third-quarter GDP growth was driven by wholesale trade, manufacturing, and finance and insurance sectors, the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said.

"Growth in the machinery, equipment & supplies segment of the wholesale trade sector, as well as the electronics and precision engineering clusters of the manufacturing sector, was boosted by strong AI-related demand," the ministry said.

For the first three quarters of the year, GDP growth was 6.2%.

The ministry now expects growth of around 6% this year, compared with its previous forecast range of 4.5% to 5.5%. For 2027, the economy is expected to grow between 2.5% and 4.5%.

However, the ministry warned of lingering downside risks to the global economy next year, citing concerns over the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence cycle. Such risks could trigger sharper corrections in global financial markets and potentially spill over into broader economic activity.

On a seasonally adjusted, quarter-over-quarter basis, GDP rose 1.5%, beating the advance estimate of 1.1% but cooling from the revised 1.8% expansion recorded in the second quarter.

data.title: Singapore raises 2026 growth forecast after 6.1% Q3 expansion
data.description:
Singapore upgraded its 2026 economic growth forecast to around 6.0% on Tuesday after posting third-quarter expansion of 6.1% from a year earlier, government data showed.

The July to September growth was higher than an official advance estimate of 5.4% and above the 5.6% expected in a Reuters poll of economists​.

On a quarter-on-quarter, seasonally adjusted basis, gross domestic product expanded by 1.5% in the July-September period, compared with an advance estimate of 1.1% growth.

The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry now expects 2027 GDP growth to come in at a range of 2.5% to 4.5%.

"Although elevated energy prices have contributed to global inflationary pressures and tighter monetary policy in several economies, on balance, METI’s assessment is that Singapore’s external demand outlook for the year has improved compared to the assessment in August," the ministry said.

In a separate statement, Enterprise Singapore upgraded its non-oil domestic exports forecast to a growth of 30% to 32% in 2026, from 14% to 16% previously.

That was driven primarily by AI-related growth in electronics and specialised machinery as well as support from lumpy exports of the structures of ships and boats.

Singapore had in August upgraded its growth forecast for this year to 4.5% to 5.5%, from a previous range of 2.0% to 4.0%, saying the impact of the Middle East war had been less severe than initially feared while the global AI investment boom had been stronger than expected.

Singapore's key consumer price gauge rose 1.5% in October from a year earlier.

Last month, the central bank kept its monetary settings unchanged in a move that surprised analysts, with inflation risks expected to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.

data.title: Waratah Minerals Delivers High-Grade Gold Assays from Drilling at Goldenclad Prospect
data.description:
Waratah Minerals has intersected broad zones of shallow high-grade gold mineralisation across multiple lodes in diamond drilling at the Goldenclad prospect within its Spur project in New South Wales.

Drilling tested beneath numerous historic gold workings to investigate the continuity of mineralisation across a high-priority six-kilometre target zone at the margin of the Cargo Intrusive Complex (CIC).

Partial results from hole GCD002 along a previously undrilled zone of outcropping mineralisation known as the Wollard’s Line returned best assays of 10 metres at 12.18 grams per tonne gold from 49m within 17m at 7.35g/t and 20.7m at 0.55g/t gold from 11.3m including 2m at 1.76g/t from 30 m.

Hole GCD003 at the Goldenclad Line delivered 7m at 2.58g/t gold from 51m within 13m at 1.51g/t from 48m, 7m at 5.66g/t gold from 85m within 28m at 1.57g/t from 84m, and 7m at 2.68g/t gold from 137m within 32.3m at 1g/t from 123m.

The district appears to contain multiple mineralised structures associated with the margins of the CIC, with recent exploration supporting the concept of a wider corridor linking Ironclad, Goldenclad, Spur, and Consols.

Scale and Potential

Executive chair Andrew Stewart said the latest results delivered high-grade gold close to surface while providing further evidence of the scale and potential of the broader Goldenclad system.

“While drilling at Goldenclad remains at an early stage, our geological team is systematically defining the controls, continuity and architecture of the mineralised system,” he said.

“GCD002 is particularly significant as the first drill test of the Wollard’s Line and has given us an exciting new high-grade result from a separate mineralised trend that remains open for further testing.”

“GCD003 was designed to test for multiple lodes within the Goldenclad Line and has intersected three significant gold zones within the top 155m.”

“These early results indicate a similar emerging theme to that observed at the Consols and Spur gold zones, being multiple gold-bearing lodes within a broader mineralised system, and provide significant scope to expand the mineralised footprint beyond the current mineral resource estimate.”

$50m Capital Raising

Waratah has received firm commitments to raise $50 million to support an ongoing exploration program aimed at growing the Spur project’s 3.1-million-ounce gold resource.

Strong demand from new and existing institutional, sophisticated, and professional investors will see the company issue 76.9 million new and fully paid ordinary shares priced at $0.65 each.

The funds will underpin more than 100,000m of drilling over the next 12 months using 12 diamond rigs to aggressively pursue resource growth.

“Our immediate focus is to convert this funding into metres drilled and then into additional ounces and ultimately build a substantially larger resource at Spur,” Mr Stewart said.

“At the same time, we will continue metallurgical and geotechnical work and broader exploration across at Ironclad, Goldenclad, Alpine, and Gazzards.”

“The strong support from existing shareholders and a select group of new and long-only global specialist resources investors is a significant endorsement of our strategy and the scale of the opportunity at Spur.”

data.title: CFTC staff advisory says crypto can count toward reserves, not liquidity rule
data.description:
Some cryptocurrency assets can count toward the reserves that trading platforms and clearinghouses must keep on hand, but not toward a separate liquidity requirement, staff at the US commodities regulator said in an advisory on Monday.

Here are the details:

  • Staff in the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued the advisory.

  • It applies to swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations.

  • The advisory addresses three CFTC regulations that require these entities to hold enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs.

  • The staff said bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins may count toward that requirement "subject to appropriate haircuts."

  • Crypto assets cannot satisfy the separate liquidity requirement because they don't qualify as cash or highly liquid securities under accounting rules, according to the advisory.

  • CFTC said the advisory only reflects the views of staff and does not create new rules or enforceable rights, is not a no-action position, and does not necessarily represent the views of the commission.
